faq_items.question: What is the best wall art for a home office?
faq_items.answer: The best home office wall art is a small coordinated set of 2-3 prints that share one color palette and type style, mixing a motivational phrase, a calming visual like line art, and a neutral accent. Cohesion reads as intentional design and holds up well on video calls.

faq_items.question: How do I print wall art at home so it looks professional?
faq_items.answer: Print on matte photo paper or 32lb cardstock rather than thin copy paper, set your printer to high quality, and use letter-size files that need no trimming. Matte avoids glare on camera, and a slim white mat inside the frame gives any printable a custom, gallery finish.

faq_items.question: What size should office wall art be above a desk?
faq_items.answer: For most desks, an 8x10 or 11x14 framed print works on the main wall, while a set of three 5x7s suits a narrow shelf. Center the arrangement at seated eye level, around 57-60 inches from the floor, so the art connects to your workspace instead of floating.

faq_items.question: How can I hang office art in a rental without damaging walls?
faq_items.answer: Use removable adhesive strips, washi tape, or a leaning shelf. Damage-free hanging strips hold framed prints securely and peel off cleanly, washi tape gives a soft no-frame look, and leaning prints on a shelf lets you rotate them in seconds with zero holes.
